reverse_outline.summary: What the part designs: messaging and leads, payments, monetization models, catalog and entitlements, advertising
Revenue is decided here; professionals renew on leads they can count, and undelivered paid products lose customers
Architectural stakes: paid products affect ranking, messages pass safety gates, invoices must reconcile with delivery

Three key points: conversation vs. lead with safety on the delivery path; unit of charge sets the architecture and spends liquidity; prove delivery through a separate catalog, price, entitlement ledger and bill
Failure patterns addressed: fraud through fast messaging, creeping paid boosts, guesswork billing
Shift from safe contact (Part V) to how a classifieds site earns: selling access to attention
Thesis: conversion and monetization are one pipeline with a built-in conflict, so every revenue line must cap its cost to the match rate
Roadmap: chapter order follows the money, plus the table, connections section and Veldmark thread
Introduces the table of chapter questions and when to read each
Links to neighbouring parts: inputs from Part V, ranking in Part IV, plumbing from Part VII, finance-book pointer
Veldmark example and the per-chapter decisions: conversation service, transaction platform, monetization proposals, Tally entitlement service, ads rules
Closing payoff: what the reader can say about any paid product, then where to start

results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All seven prose units' outline summaries match the controlling ideas of their aligned spec paragraphs (p01-p07) in the same order; the five callouts are house format and match nothing in the paragraph list.
Marked two_ideas, but the KEY POINTS callout is the house format's three-bullet statement of the part's claim; each bullet carries one idea and the callout is not a prose paragraph.
Marked two_ideas (chapter order plus the sections that follow), but both halves serve the one roadmap idea the spec gives p03: the page's reading plan.
p01-p03 state the hook, claim and order; p04 supports PVI-1, p05 PVI-2, p06 PVI-3; p07 synthesizes. No unit is off-thesis.

The figure in p02 sits in a paragraph that states what it shows (revenue lines capped against the match rate); the table is introduced by 'Each row gives a chapter's question and when to open it'; the Veldmark decisions are framed 'per chapter' and the Tally bullet carries the overbilling cost. The city bike and Golf are named as the recurring cases only, which the spec does not ask them to prove (see the minor flow finding).
problem_solution: from charging for attention to 'The argument of this part is that conversion and monetization are one pipeline with a conflict built in', then the capping answer.
elaboration: 'These chapters design each revenue line...' is carried into 'Chapters follow the money in the order it arises'.
elaboration: the roadmap's 'A table says when to open each chapter' is kept by 'Each row gives a chapter's question and when to open it'.

results.quote: a section places the part between Parts IV, V and VII
results.finding: Reader A: 'You cannot sit between three things; re-read.' The sentence misdescribes the connection section, which takes threads from Parts V and IV and needs Part VII (reader B: the section takes the parts in order V, IV, VII, not matching the roadmap; the AC-4 reader flagged the same slip). The order is sound; the wording obscures it.

results.quote: For the payments and ledger depth behind Tradeyard Safe Deal, see the sibling finance book's [[payments-fundamentals]].
results.finding: Reader A calls this 'the clearest out-of-place moment': Tradeyard Safe Deal is named before the Veldmark section and 'the sibling finance book' comes out of nowhere. The section order is the house shape and works; the sentence needs a gloss (whose Safe Deal, which sibling book) or a home in the Veldmark section.

results.draft_locus: Introduction callout (KEY POINTS); Introduction ¶2; Where to begin ¶1
results.quote: so attention is sold without selling out liquidity
results.finding: Both readers could not tie 'liquidity' (KEY POINTS 'every model spends liquidity', the closing) to 'match rate' (thesis paragraph); reader A: 'Liquidity and match rate never tied together'. The terms are in the audience's already_knows, but the page switches between them without saying how they relate, so a reader must infer it. One clause in p02 would fix it.

results.quote: reconcile delivery events from insertion (a paid listing going live), ranking, rendering, lead routing and ad serving against grants and invoices
results.finding: Reader A: 'Parenthetical inside a five-item list made me re-read.' Reader B: the bullet packs a five-item list, a bracket gloss and the undefined 'grants'. The bullet is overloaded.
results.corroborated_by: flowA, item A7 / flowB, item B3

results.quote: Femke's Rotterdam city bike, sold for €225 through Tradeyard Safe Deal, and a Volkswagen Golf in Essen with 23 raw leads (19 once repeat contacts are merged) carry the thread.
results.finding: Reader A only: the bullets never mention the bike or the Golf again, so 'carry the thread' promises a link the section does not show. Reader B called the raw-lead figure an acceptable teaser (B8), a different point.

results.finding: Reader A only: the entry reads as if the failure pattern puts the gate in place rather than the part's answer to it.

results.quote: then the payment that closes the deal
results.finding: Reader A only: tension with 'A classifieds site usually steps aside before the sale'; resolved later by the table row, and the reader names it only as a brief stumble.

results.quote: The marketplace earns its core revenue when buyers find the right listing quickly.
results.finding: Reader B only: briefly clashed with 'charges for access to attention' from ¶1; the link (professionals renew on leads they can count) is in a callout, not in the thesis paragraph.

results.quote: one group conversation service with a message safety gate (May 2027), live for Tradeyard NL and BE in November 2027
results.finding: Reader A only: unsure whether 'May 2027' dates the gate or the decision. Minor.

results.quote: Safe Deal Portugal approved for Q3 2028 on it
results.finding: Reader B only: 'on it' reaches back across a colon and is hard to parse; the dense dates briefly read as a timeline.

'Grants' (an entitlement term owned by products-and-entitlements, on does_not_know) is used without a gloss; the page glosses Tally and names the entitlement ledger but never says what a grant is. Other terms pass: liquidity, match rate, relevance floor, DAC7, Tradeyard Safe Deal, Motorvane, Hearthly and Ingrid Halvorsen are in already_knows; conversation, lead, unit of charge and entitlement are glossed in KEY POINTS; header bidding and ad load appear only in the table's 'Read it when' column, as the spec allows.
Opens with a direct statement that bridges from Part V and names what a classifieds site sells; none of placeholder, restated question, dictionary, 'dawn of man' or book report.
Short synthesis, the part's test and the hand-off; no new idea, no 'in conclusion', no body evidence, not a rephrased thesis alone.

'The chapters give every revenue line a record both sides can count, proof of delivery and a guardrail on the match rate' synthesizes; the so-what is the test a reader can apply to any paid product, then 'Begin with [[messaging-and-leads]]'.
'so attention is sold without selling out liquidity' returns to ¶1's 'it charges for access to attention'.

results.quote: then the revenue models and the record of what sellers bought
results.finding: The roadmap promises five chapters, but the intro reader listed four positions and could not tell 'whether monetization models and catalog/entitlement ledger are one chapter or two; how many chapters'. Order, the remaining sections, evidence and tone were predicted correctly. The roadmap sentence joins chapters 3 and 4 in one clause and never says 'five'.

The reader named all five chapters in order with the question each answers, matching expected (messaging and leads; transactions and payments; monetization models; products and entitlements; advertising platforms).
lead counts -> messaging-and-leads; disputed invoice -> products-and-entitlements; header-bidding timeout -> advertising-platforms, as expected.

The reader named Part V's three threads, Part IV's ranking and relevance floor, and Part VII's events, governed metric and guardrailed tests, as expected; the roadmap wording slip it noted is recorded under flow_is_followable.
